newsitem.title: THAILAND: Investors besiege new Thai stocks support fund.
newsitem.headline: Investors besiege new Thai stocks support fund.

text.p: Financially-strapped Thai investors besieged a 10 billion baht (US$400 million) stock market support fund launched by the government on the first day it opened to borrowers, an official said on Tuesday.
Government Savings Bank president Boonyarak Ningsanond told reporters investors on Monday hads applied for all of the 10 billion baht available through state-owned bank's fund.
Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda said on Tuesday the government had no immediate plan to enlarge the fund to accommodate further loan demand from small investors.
He said he would instruct the bank to try to spread the fund evenly among the applicants. He did not elaborate.
Boonyarak said earlier his bank would start signing loan contracts on September 26. Borrowers would be charged an 11 percent lending rate and additional percentage points as a service fee.
He said loan disbursement was expected to start from September 30.
The fund will extend loans to investors to help them meet margin calls and avoid being forced to sell shares at big losses to pay off debts.
It is the second rescue fund launched by government and private sectors in the past six weeks to shore the Thai bourse which last week dropped near three-year-lows.
A separate 15.7 billion baht fund started by commercial banks and brokerage houses has already entered the market and has been buying shares since September 6. (US$1 = 25 baht)
